Revenue Ops is complaining that the same CRM problem has been reported several times and nobody is picking it up. You are the planning step. You have no tools here: think the task through and write the plan only.

Produce an ordered list of at most 8 steps for an executor who will have the full toolset. Each step must be one concrete action, specific enough to carry out without guessing, and must include any check that has to happen before it. Add a short rationale for the approach.

toolInput.rationale: Ticket consolidation requires first gathering evidence (current CRM ticket list and each ticket's actual content) before deciding which are true duplicates, since only genuinely identical incidents may be merged per policy. Severity and routing must be derived from the escalation matrix and resolved on-call at the correct instant (the merged deadline), not guessed, and the survivor must be the earliest-created ticket carrying the earliest SLA deadline.
steps: Call get_current_time and list_tickets filtered to service=crm and status=open (and also status=new if present) to get the full candidate set.

Call get_ticket on each open/new CRM ticket to read its description, impact scope, creation time, and existing SLA deadline, to determine which ones describe the same underlying problem versus a different issue.
Call get_escalation_matrix for service=crm to see the severity-per-impact-scope table and the response target / escalation rotation for each severity, so grading is policy-based not guessed.

Group the tickets that are truly the same incident (same root cause/symptom, not just same service); select the earliest-created ticket among them as the survivor, and identify its earliest SLA deadline (or the earliest deadline across the set if any already have one committed).

Call merge_tickets with survivorId set to the earliest-created ticket, duplicateIds set to the rest of the confirmed-duplicate group, and slaDueAt set to the earliest deadline in the set (or, if none has a deadline yet, the current time plus the response target for the severity that will be assigned).
Determine the correct severity for the survivor from the escalation matrix using its (now broadest) impact scope, and call set_severity with that value.
Call get_oncall for the CRM-owning rotation named in the escalation matrix, with `at` set explicitly to the survivor's SLA deadline, to find the correct engineer at that instant.

Call assign_ticket to assign the survivor to that on-call engineer, then post_comment on the survivor summarizing which tickets were merged into it and why, leaving any non-duplicate CRM tickets untouched.
